<div class="sheet">
  <div class="ws-head"><div><h1>PROSE Readiness Assessment and Remediation Plan</h1><p class="ws-sub">A dated PROSE scorecard per repository or team, plus a remediation backlog ordered by blast radius. Surface A of four: the eleven-question compliance checklist.</p></div>
  <div class="ws-meta"><b>WS-13-prose-readiness-assessment</b><br>Pack Z - Second wave: the practitioner kit<br>fill order <b>7</b> &middot; type <b>rubric</b><br>audience <b>mixed</b></div></div>
  <div class="ws-source">Source: <b>The PROSE Constraints</b>, <i>Compliance Checklist</i> &middot; <code>handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.qmd</code> L535-565 &middot; <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.html#sec-prose-compliance-checklist">#sec-prose-compliance-checklist</a></div>
  <div class="ws-instruction">Answer each of the eleven yes/no questions below, Pass or Fail, with evidence: a file path for every Pass, a named counter-example file for every Fail. Name an owner and a target date for every Fail. Fail on S1, S2 or S3 means start there, whatever else you find. If the shadow-AI census found little, defer this surface and write DEFERRED across it &mdash; do not mark it passed. Surfaces A and B are filled live; B follows on sheet 2.</div>

    <tbody>

    <div class="prior" style="margin-top:2mm"><b>Remediation bands (the book's own, not re-ordered).</b> <b>Band 1 = S1, S2, S3</b> &mdash; start here regardless of total score; highest blast radius and fastest to close (one YAML change per agent). <b>Band 2 = E1, E2</b> &mdash; address next; fastest architectural change (create two scoped files and you have three levels). <b>Band 3 = P1, P2, R1, R2, O1, O2</b> &mdash; discipline and refactoring; prioritise the constraint that maps to your current failure mode: scope creep, fix R1/R2; context dilution, fix P1/P2; debugging nightmares, fix O1/O2.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L555-559</span></div>

<div class="sheet">
  <div class="ws-head"><div><h1>PROSE Readiness Assessment and Remediation Plan</h1><p class="ws-sub">Surface B: the five-constraint rollup and executive-reporting layer. Surface D: the structural-properties control map, filled last.</p></div>
  <div class="ws-meta"><b>WS-13-prose-readiness-assessment</b><br>Pack Z - Second wave: the practitioner kit<br>fill order <b>7</b> &middot; type <b>rubric</b><br>audience <b>mixed</b></div></div>
  <div class="ws-source">Source: <b>The PROSE Constraints</b>, <i>Compliance Checklist</i> &middot; <code>handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.qmd</code> L535-565 &middot; <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.html#sec-prose-compliance-checklist">#sec-prose-compliance-checklist</a></div>
  <div class="ws-instruction">For each PROSE constraint, say whether today's practice is absent, ad hoc, documented or enforced, and name the file, gate, job or policy that satisfies it. Tick every anti-pattern you currently exhibit and give one concrete example for each tick &mdash; a file, a prompt, an agent configuration or a session. A constraint may be called enforced only if every checklist item rolled into it passed on sheet 1. Then, at the end, name the specific control for each structural property, its owner and how it is verified.</div>
  <div class="ws-block"><h2>B &mdash; Constraint rollup <span class="ws-block-note">one row per constraint; no weighting across constraints, no score</span></h2>
    <table class="ws"><colgroup><col style="width:3%"><col style="width:9%"><col style="width:13%"><col style="width:13%"><col style="width:14%"><col style="width:7%"><col style="width:17%"><col style="width:7%"><col style="width:17%"></colgroup>
    <thead><tr><th></th><th>Constraint</th><th>Addresses / Induces</th><th>Today's practice</th><th>Artefact or control that satisfies it</th><th>Checklist items rolling up</th><th>Matching anti-pattern (the book)</th><th>Tick</th><th>One example of the anti-pattern &mdash; mandatory when ticked</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
<tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">15</span></td><td class="prior"><b>Progressive Disclosure</b><span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22</span></td>
<td class="prior">Addresses: Context overload. Induces: Efficient context utilization.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22; ch01 L63-69</span></td>
<td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">absent</span><span class="opt">ad hoc</span><span class="opt">documented</span><span class="opt">enforced</span></div></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
<td class="prior">P1, P2<span class="prior-src">ch13 L541-551</span></td>
<td class="prior"><b>Context dumping</b> &mdash; Everything loaded upfront; wastes capacity; dilutes attention on what matters<span class="prior-src">ch01 L112-118</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>exhibited</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td></tr>
<tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">16</span></td><td class="prior"><b>Reduced Scope</b><span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22</span></td>
<td class="prior">Addresses: Scope creep. Induces: Manageable complexity.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22; ch01 L63-69</span></td>
<td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">absent</span><span class="opt">ad hoc</span><span class="opt">documented</span><span class="opt">enforced</span></div></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
<td class="prior">R1, R2<span class="prior-src">ch13 L541-551</span></td>
<td class="prior"><b>Scope creep</b> &mdash; Task grows mid-session; agent loses track of earlier instructions as attention degrades<span class="prior-src">ch01 L112-118</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>exhibited</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td></tr>
<tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">17</span></td><td class="prior"><b>Orchestrated Composition</b><span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22</span></td>
<td class="prior">Addresses: Monolithic collapse. Induces: Flexibility, reusability.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22; ch01 L63-69</span></td>
<td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">absent</span><span class="opt">ad hoc</span><span class="opt">documented</span><span class="opt">enforced</span></div></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
<td class="prior">O1, O2<span class="prior-src">ch13 L541-551</span></td>
<td class="prior"><b>Monolithic prompt</b> &mdash; All instructions in one block; small changes produce unpredictable results; impossible to debug<span class="prior-src">ch01 L112-118</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>exhibited</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td></tr>
<tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">18</span></td><td class="prior"><b>Safety Boundaries</b><span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22</span></td>
<td class="prior">Addresses: Unbounded autonomy. Induces: Reliability, verifiability.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22; ch01 L63-69</span></td>
<td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">absent</span><span class="opt">ad hoc</span><span class="opt">documented</span><span class="opt">enforced</span></div></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
<td class="prior">S1, S2, S3<span class="prior-src">ch13 L541-551</span></td>
<td class="prior"><b>Unbounded agent</b> &mdash; No limits on tools or authority; non-determinism plus unlimited access equals unpredictable behavior<span class="prior-src">ch01 L112-118</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>exhibited</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td></tr>
<tr><td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">19</span></td><td class="prior"><b>Explicit Hierarchy</b><span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22</span></td>
<td class="prior">Addresses: Flat guidance. Induces: Modularity, domain adaptation.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L16-22; ch01 L63-69</span></td>
<td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">absent</span><span class="opt">ad hoc</span><span class="opt">documented</span><span class="opt">enforced</span></div></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
<td class="prior">E1, E2<span class="prior-src">ch13 L541-551</span></td>
<td class="prior"><b>Flat instructions</b> &mdash; Same rules everywhere; backend security rules load when editing frontend CSS<span class="prior-src">ch01 L112-118</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>exhibited</span></td>
<td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td></tr>

    </tbody></table>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-head"><div><h1>PROSE Readiness Assessment and Remediation Plan</h1><p class="ws-sub">Surface C: the file-by-file disclosure and refactor inventory, one row per existing instruction file, skill, persona and prompt. Prepare it before the session; the full list lives in your spreadsheet.</p></div>
  <div class="ws-meta"><b>WS-13-prose-readiness-assessment</b><br>Pack Z - Second wave: the practitioner kit<br>fill order <b>7</b> &middot; type <b>rubric</b><br>audience <b>mixed</b></div></div>
  <div class="ws-source">Source: <b>The PROSE Constraints</b>, <i>Compliance Checklist</i> &middot; <code>handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.qmd</code> L535-565 &middot; <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch13-the-prose-specification.html#sec-prose-compliance-checklist">#sec-prose-compliance-checklist</a></div>
  <div class="ws-instruction">Before the session, run a line count across the estate and list every existing instruction file, skill, persona and prompt, one per row. Tick both size tests for every file, list the subsidiary topics inlined by heading, name the file each should be extracted to, and give an owner and target date for every action other than none. Fill in the header on sheet 1 first. Continue in the spreadsheet if you run out of rows.</div>
  <div class="ws-block"><h2>C &mdash; Disclosure and refactor inventory <span class="ws-block-note">one row per primitive file</span></h2>
    <div class="prior"><b>C3 &mdash; a design target (ch12).</b> "If your instruction file exceeds 40-50 lines, it's trying to do too much," because every line of instruction competes for attention with the source code the agent needs to read.<span class="prior-src">ch12 L74</span></div>
    <div class="prior" style="margin-top:1.5mm"><b>C4 &mdash; a hard trigger (ch13, checklist item P1).</b> Does every instruction file over 100 lines use links, not inline content, for subsidiary topics?<span class="prior-src">ch13 L541</span></div>
    <div class="prior" style="margin-top:1.5mm"><b>C5, C6, C7, C9 &mdash; the chapter's worked example.</b> Before: five inlined sections (coding standards, authentication, error handling, deployment, accessibility). After: five pointers with descriptive labels, e.g. "Authentication patterns and token lifecycle", not <code>auth.md</code> &mdash; same information, a fraction of the context cost per task. Extraction targets look like <code>./standards/auth.md</code>.<span class="prior-src">ch13 L81-104</span></div>
    <div class="prior" style="margin:1.5mm 0 2mm"><i>The book states 40-50 lines (ch12) and 100 lines (ch13, checklist item P1) in different chapters without reconciling them. This sheet records both, as two different tests. The intended reading is an open question for the author.</i></div>
